question: ok real talk, how do i poop in the woods
keyPoints: Dig a small hole (a cathole) about 6-8 inches deep and cover it afterwards
Go well away from water, trails and camp (about 200 feet / 70 steps)
Pack out toilet paper, or use none, rather than leaving it
redFlags: Leave toilet paper on the ground
Go near a stream or lake

question: where am i supposed to pee when we're camping
keyPoints: Well away from water sources and camp (about 200 feet)
Away from the trail; in some places urinating on rock or bare ground rather than plants is advised

question: got my period on a 3 day backpacking trip, what do i do with used pads and tampons
keyPoints: Pack them out in a sealed bag
Don't bury them or leave them

question: how do i pick a good spot to pitch the tent
keyPoints: Use an established site or durable ground (rock, gravel, dry grass) rather than fragile plants
Camp well back from lakes and streams (about 200 feet)
Avoid hazards: low spots that collect water, and dead trees or branches overhead

question: how do i keep bears out of my food overnight
keyPoints: Store food in a bear canister/locker or hang it, as local rules require
Keep food, cooking and scented items (toothpaste, trash) away from where you sleep

question: whats the right way to wash dishes when backpacking
keyPoints: Wash well away from streams and lakes (about 200 feet), not in them
Use little or no soap; strain out food scraps and pack them out, scatter the dishwater
redFlags: Wash dishes with soap directly in a stream or lake

question: how should i dress for a cold hike, i always end up sweaty then freezing
keyPoints: Dress in layers: a base layer that wicks moisture, an insulating layer, and a wind/waterproof shell
Take layers off before you sweat and add them when you stop
Avoid cotton, which stays wet and cold

question: i froze all night in my sleeping bag, how do i sleep warmer
keyPoints: Insulate from the ground with a sleeping pad; the ground steals heat
Sleep in dry clothes, not the damp ones you hiked in
Eat something and stay hydrated before bed; wear a hat

question: new boots, long hike this weekend, how do i not get destroyed by blisters
keyPoints: Break new boots in on shorter walks first
Wear well-fitting moisture-wicking socks (not cotton) and keep feet dry
Stop and cover hot spots with tape or moleskin before they become blisters

question: how much water should i bring on a day hike
keyPoints: It depends on heat, effort and length: bring more than you think and drink regularly
Know where refills are, and treat water from natural sources before drinking

question: we're allowed a campfire tonight, anything i should know
keyPoints: Check current fire restrictions; use an existing fire ring and keep the fire small
Burn only dead and down wood, never cut live trees
Put it out completely: drown, stir, and feel that it's cold before leaving
redFlags: Leave a fire smouldering or unattended

question: who's supposed to step aside on a narrow trail, the people going up or down
keyPoints: Hikers going uphill generally have the right of way
Everyone yields to horses/pack stock; bikes yield to hikers

question: a group on horses is coming toward us on the trail what do we do
keyPoints: Step off the trail, usually on the downhill side, and let them pass
Stay calm and visible, speak to the riders, no sudden movements

question: how do i pack my backpack so it doesnt kill my shoulders
keyPoints: Put heavy items in the middle, close to your back
Keep often-needed items (water, snacks, rain jacket) where you can reach them
Adjust the hip belt so the hips carry most of the weight

question: are trekking poles actually worth it
keyPoints: They take strain off knees, especially going downhill
They help balance on rough ground and stream crossings

question: my knees hurt so bad on the way down every hike, any tricks
keyPoints: Take shorter steps and keep knees slightly bent
Trekking poles help take load off the knees on descents
Go slowly; don't run or lock the knees

question: what should always be in my pack even for a short hike
keyPoints: The ten essentials: navigation, light, sun protection, first aid, knife, fire starter, shelter, extra food, extra water, extra clothes

question: going solo this weekend, anything i should do before i leave
keyPoints: Tell someone where you're going and when you'll be back (leave an itinerary)
Check the weather and conditions, and carry the essentials

question: afternoon storms keep rolling in on our mountain trip, how do we plan around that
keyPoints: Start early and be off peaks, ridges and exposed high ground before storms build in the afternoon
If you hear thunder, head down and away from summits and lone tall trees
redFlags: Shelter under a lone tall tree

question: how do i keep my sleeping bag dry if it rains all day
keyPoints: Line the pack with a waterproof bag (pack liner or trash bag) and keep the bag inside it
A pack cover alone isn't enough; keep wet gear separate from dry sleeping clothes

question: ticks are everywhere where we hike, how do i keep them off
keyPoints: Wear long pants tucked into socks and use repellent
Check your whole body after the hike and remove any tick promptly

question: how long will a 10 mile hike with 3000 feet of climbing take me
keyPoints: Allow extra time for climbing on top of distance (e.g. roughly 2 mph plus about an hour per 1,000 feet)
Set a turnaround time and stick to it

question: how close can i get to elk for a good photo
keyPoints: Keep a safe distance (NPS: at least 25 yards from most animals, 100 yards from bears and wolves)
Use a zoom lens; if the animal changes its behaviour you're too close; never feed wildlife

question: can i just toss my apple core into the bushes, it's biodegradable right
keyPoints: No: pack it out; food scraps take a long time to break down and teach animals to seek human food
redFlags: Throwing food scraps away is fine

question: it's pouring, can we just cook inside the tent
keyPoints: Don't cook inside a tent: carbon monoxide can kill and the tent can catch fire
Cook outside or under a tarp/vestibule with good airflow, away from the tent body
redFlags: Cooking inside a closed tent is fine

question: hiking in the desert next week, any tips for the heat
keyPoints: Hike early or late and rest in shade in the heat of the day
Carry plenty of water and salty snacks, and drink regularly
Wear sun protection: hat, light long sleeves, sunscreen

question: we camped by the creek at the bottom of the valley and it was freezing, why
keyPoints: Cold air sinks and collects in valley bottoms at night
Camping a little higher on a bench or slope is usually warmer (and keeps you back from the water)

question: my feet are always soaked and wrinkly by the end of the day
keyPoints: Change into dry socks, and let feet air out at breaks
Wear moisture-wicking (wool/synthetic) socks, not cotton

question: stepped in a hole on the trail, my ankle is swelling up fast and i cant put any weight on it
keyPoints: Stop and don't walk on it; support/splint it if it may be broken
Cool it, compress it and raise it
Get help or evacuate if they can't bear weight

question: my buddy's shivering like crazy and slurring his words after we got soaked in the rain
keyPoints: Get him out of the wind and wet clothes into dry insulation, off the ground
Warm sweet drinks if he's alert; warm the core, handle gently
Get help

question: we were cooking in the tent and now my girlfriend has a pounding headache and feels dizzy
keyPoints: Get her into fresh air immediately and turn off the stove
This could be carbon monoxide poisoning: get medical help, especially if she gets worse or confused
redFlags: Stay in the tent and rest

question: my friend stopped sweating, his skin is really hot and he's confused on this hike
keyPoints: This is heat stroke: an emergency
Cool him immediately (shade, water on skin, fanning, cold packs at neck/armpits/groin)
Get emergency help
redFlags: Wait to see if it passes

question: got stung by a bee and now my throat feels tight and my lips are swelling
keyPoints: Possible anaphylaxis: use an epinephrine auto-injector if available
Get emergency help immediately
redFlags: Just take it easy and wait

question: lightning hit right near us and my friend is on the ground not breathing
keyPoints: It's safe to touch them
Start CPR and get emergency help
